use_case_name: Share a Geographic Pointer with Other Units

claims.content: A J7.3 message provides the capability for C² JUs to designate a geographic position and up to twenty characters of text on one or more C² JU's displays.

goal.raw_text: A J7.3 message provides the capability for C² JUs to designate a geographic position and up to twenty characters of text on one or more C² JU's displays.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU must have the capability to generate and transmit a J7.3 message.
The C2 JU operator initiates the sharing of a geographic pointer by generating and transmitting a J7.3 message to designate a position and optional text on other units’ displays.

trigger.raw_text: The C2 JU operator initiates the sharing of a geographic pointer by generating and transmitting a J7.3 message to designate a position and optional text on other units’ displays.

claims.content: The C2 JU operator generates and transmits a J7.3 message to designate a geographic position.
The message may include up to twenty characters of optional textual clarification.
The message is addressed to one, multiple, or all Information Units (IUs) using specific address words (J7.3I, J7.3C1).
Upon receipt, the designated geographic position and text are displayed on the receiving C2 JU's displays.
If no textual clarification is included in the J7.3 message, it must be used in conjunction with voice communications to convey intent.
When addressing a single JU, the J7.3I Pointer initial word contains the specific address of that unit.

When addressing multiple JUs, the J7.3I word contains one address and the J7.3C1 continuation word can contain up to four additional addresses; multiple J7.3C1 words may be sent for more than five addresses.
When addressing all JUs, the J7.3I word contains the collective address instead of individual unit addresses.
The designated geographic position and optional text (up to twenty characters) are displayed on the receiving C2 JU's displays.
Since no Track Number (TN) is assigned to the pointer, the displayed pointer must be managed (displayed and dropped) by local procedure.
